﻿# Authorized penetration test — milenkih-team tennis app

You are authorized by the application owner to pentest this target. Do NOT modify, rewrite, delete, or create any source files in the mounted workspace. Read-only analysis of code. Exploitation only against the live target URL.

## Targets
- Live app: https://app.milenkih-team.ru (React frontend inside MAX messenger + PocketBase Go/SQLite backend)
- Local source: mounted workspace (white-box). READ ONLY — never edit files.

## Auth (user role, NOT moderator)
Send on all authenticated API requests:
Header name: Authorization
Header value: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJjb2xsZWN0aW9uSWQiOiJfcGJfdXNlcnNfYXV0aF8iLCJleHAiOjE3ODk4MjkzNTAsImlkIjoiaHFkNDJ0djloMDg1Yms1IiwicmVmcmVzaGFibGUiOnRydWUsInR5cGUiOiJhdXRoIn0.UZRN8FJ3nh3vAS3rAflLjNRYeS9p-awDLWzbBHiOKE8

PocketBase typically expects: Authorization: <token> (sometimes Bearer <token>). Try both if one fails.
Authenticated user id from JWT: hqd42tv9h085bk5

## Coverage requirements (map findings to categories)

### 1) OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) — PocketBase API
- Enumerate /api/ collections, auth, files, realtime
- API1 BOLA/IDOR: access other users' records by id
- API3 Broken object property level authz: mass assignment / over-exposure on list/view
- API5 Broken function-level authz: user token calling moderator/admin-only routes
- Injection, auth/token flaws, unrestricted resource consumption

### 2) Web app pentest — React inside MAX
- Auth bypass, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, business logic
- Client-side trust of role/moderator flags
- Sensitive data in responses, localStorage, frontend config

### 3) OWASP Top 10:2025
Cover systematically; map each finding to A01–A10 (2025 edition).
Prioritize A01 access control/SSRF, A02 misconfig, A05 injection, A07 auth failures, A10 exceptional conditions.
State honestly if A09 cannot be assessed from outside.

### 4) White-box code review
Focus on: client/src/services/*, pb_hooks/*, auth, admin, achievements.
Especially achievements security holes:
- client/src/services/achievements.js
- client/src/hooks/useAchievements.js
- pb_hooks/achievementslib.js
- AchievementsBlock, FloatingAchievements, StatsAchievementsModal
Check: client-side-only progress calc that can be forged; missing server rules; IDOR on achievement/level records; privilege escalation via updating achievement fields; forging tournament places/wins/rating/attendance stats.

## Out of scope
- Do not spam mass notifications/broadcasts to real users
- Do not destroy production data (prefer create+cleanup test records)
- Do not modify mounted source files

## Reporting
Only report validated findings with working PoC (exact request/response). Severity critical/high/medium/low/info.

FOCUS: achievements / rating / statistics integrity, both client-side and server-side. Read these files first and quote exact line numbers in your findings:
- client/src/services/achievements.js (progress computed CLIENT-SIDE from users.rating_points, users.attendance_count, and tournament_posts.participants JSON)
- client/src/hooks/useAchievements.js
- pb_hooks/achievementslib.js
- pb_hooks/postslib.js (applyTournamentRating — awards rating_points from tournament_posts.participants[].points)
- client/src/components/.../ AchievementsBlock, FloatingAchievements, StatsAchievementsModal (find them)
Key question set:
1. Can a plain `user` (role=user, id hqd42tv9h085bk5) write ANY of the client-trusted values directly? Enumerate every source: rating_points, attendance_count (users collection), tournament_posts.participants (moderator-only?), content_views rows, notifications rows. For each, try to write it and record the exact response.
2. `content_views`: createRule is `@request.auth.id != "" && user = @request.auth.id` with NO list/view rule. Can a user POST arbitrary rows with any object_type/object_id/source to inflate view counters? What consumes content_views (read pb_hooks/stats.pb.js and client/src/hooks/usePostViewTracker.js) and does the inflation have a visible effect anywhere? Is there a uniqueness/dedup rule you can bypass, and is there unbounded resource consumption (post thousands of rows)? Do a SMALL bounded test (e.g. 20 rows) with marker values, then delete them.
3. `notifications`: createRule allows a user to create a notification addressed to themselves with attacker-chosen title/body/meta/click_action/badge_dynamic_type/training_id/training_state. Test whether such rows render in the UI (XSS / phishing surface) and whether delete/update rules let a user tamper with notifications. Also test whether `recipient` can be set to ANOTHER user id (rule says recipient = auth OR role=moderator → should fail; verify).
4. Can a user grant themselves achievement levels? achievements/achievement_levels have moderator-only write rules — verify with a real PATCH/POST attempt and record the 403.
5. Progress forgery chain: is there any server endpoint that persists achievement state (`_achievements`? a custom /api route in pb_hooks)? Grep pb_hooks for custom routerAdd endpoints and test each with the user token for BFLA.
Report validated findings with exact request/response evidence. IMPORTANT: keep any created rows bounded and delete them afterwards (marker prefix `zqath3`). Never modify real users' records beyond restoring original values. Record record_coverage for each surface. Return the write-up to the parent via agent_finish.

POST /api/max-auth, POST /api/content-view, GET /api/stats/growth, /api/stats/reach, /api/stats/reach/users, /api/stats/booking, /api/stats/trainings-count, /api/stats/growth/day, /api/stats/trainings-count/day, /api/stats/achievements, /api/stats/achievements/grants, POST /api/users-claim-max, POST /api/users-unclaim-max, GET /api/users-claim-candidates, POST /api/users-delete, POST /api/users-create-manual, POST /api/admin-backup, POST /api/internal/backup-notify, POST /api/admin-dispatch-now, POST /api/bot-notify-training, /api/bot-notify-training-status, /api/bot-notify-training-edit, /api/bot-notify-training-create, /api/bot-notify-training-cancelled, /api/bot-notify-training-restored, POST /api/max-bot-webhook, POST /api/notify-comment-reply, POST /api/audit-buy-click, GET /api/video-poster, POST /api/yadisk-preview, GET /api/yadisk-content, GET /api/system-templates, POST /api/system-templates-update, POST /api/bot-notify-membership-frozen, POST /api/notify-membership-topup.
CRITICAL RULES:
- Do NOT mass-notify or broadcast to real users. For bot/notification endpoints, test ONLY with a nonexistent training/comment id or an id you create yourself (marker prefix `zqath3`) so the call fails before reaching the MAX API, OR verify the auth gate returns 403 before any side effect. If a route would message real users, STOP at the authorization check (403/401/200 response body) and do not pass a real id.

Record exact status codes.
- Check HTTP method overrides (X-HTTP-Method-Override), trailing-slash variants, and case variants for endpoints that should be moderator-only.
Clean up anything you create (marker `zqath3`). Record coverage per route and return a precise write-up via agent_finish: route, method, auth state, status, response snippet, and whether it is a real privilege boundary violation.

Target: live PocketBase API https://app.milenkih-team.ru + read-only source /workspace/tennis (NEVER edit source files).
Call get_threat_model("https://app.milenkih-team.ru") and read the shared recon note.

Read: pb_hooks/max-auth.pb.js, pb_hooks/maxauthlib.js, pb_hooks/users_ban_auth.pb.js, pb_hooks/users_manual.pb.js, pb_hooks/users_delete.pb.js, pb_hooks/users_default_visible.pb.js, client/src/services/auth.js, client/src/hooks/useMaxAuth.js, client/src/context/*, client/src/services/pb.js, client/src/services/pocketbase.js.
Test and document with exact raw requests/responses:
1. POST /api/max-auth — the MAX Bridge signature validation. Read maxauthlib.js and determine exactly how initData is validated (HMAC-SHA256 with the bot token? constant-time compare? expiry check? user id derivation?). Test with: missing initData, empty hash, tampered hash, an initData whose user id you control (e.g. re-sign with a guessed key is out of scope, but TEST whether the server accepts an unsigned/partially-verified payload, whether it trusts client-supplied `user.id` when auth_date is fresh, and whether the `MAX_BOT_TOKEN` from client/.env (f9LHodD0cOJDcZ1AhjMzhpcQOULnrqDkScxVEsSFGrLFdBhUhcW8tqgSWO4gl5Ri54GH6OUt-v_kiSFV-PMs==) validates signatures you generate — that would be a full auth bypass). If it validates with that token, PROVE it by minting a valid initData for an arbitrary max_id and logging in as that (pick a user id that already exists, e.g. max_id 239756993 is your own — do NOT attempt to take over another real user's account; instead prove the primitive by generating a signature the server accepts and showing the response, then stop).
2. JWT: the auth token is HS256 signed with the PB app secret. Test alg=none / alg confusion, tampered payload (role: "moderator", id of another user), expired tokens, and whether the server honours the token after any logout/rotation. You cannot forge HS256 without the secret — but VERIFY that the server properly rejects forged signatures rather than trusting the payload (negative control) and record the exact rejection.
3. Auth collection endpoints: `/api/collections/users/auth-with-password` (is it enabled? test a few wrong passwords — do NOT brute force broadly, max ~10 attempts), `/auth-refresh`, `/request-otp`/`auth-with-otp`, `/request-password-reset`/`confirm-password-reset`, `/auth-with-oauth2`, `/impersonate` (superuser-only?) — record which are enabled and whether any leaks account existence (user enumeration via differing error codes/messages/timing).
4. Banned/frozen users: read users_ban_auth.pb.js — does an already-issued token still work after is_banned flips true? (Static analysis + reason about it; you cannot flip your own is_banned.) Note it as a code-level finding.
5. CORS/CSRF: inspect the nginx configs in /workspace/tennis/config/* and the live response headers (`curl -si -X OPTIONS` with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method) to determine whether PocketBase is reachable cross-origin from an arbitrary site, and whether auth is cookie-based or header-based (header = not CSRF-able via simple form post). Test `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reflection and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`.
Record coverage per surface. Report exact evidence and return a precise write-up via agent_finish.

Target: live https://app.milenkih-team.ru (React SPA in the MAX webview) + read-only source /workspace/tennis/client (NEVER edit source files).

You may also need a browser session: use `agent-browser --session frontend-xss` (see the tooling/agent_browser skill) and note the app is a MAX Mini App — it will run without the MAX bridge, falling back to localStorage authStore. 502s from the API are transient; retry.
Your focus is the WEB-APP layer (OWASP A03 XSS / A01 client-side access control / A02 misconfig):
1. Stored XSS: enumerate every place user-controlled content is rendered. Grep the client for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `eval(`, `new Function`, `srcdoc`, and any markdown/HTML renderer. Follow the data: `posts.content`, `tournament_posts.content`, comments (comments/gallery_comments/tournament_comments `content`), `full_name`, `ban_reason`, `comment_restriction_reason`, `membership_comment`, training `location`/`description`, product names/params, notification `title`/`body`/`badge_text`/`meta`, `system_message_templates`.
2. Determine which of those fields a LOW-PRIVILEGE user can set. Self-settable: users.full_name, users.avatar_url, comments.content, gallery_comments.content, tournament_comments.content, notifications.* (self-addressed). If any such value is rendered as raw HTML anywhere, that is stored XSS — prove it end-to-end and capture the exact rendering path with file:line references, and (where possible) a live DOM proof using agent-browser evaluate on the real page.
3. `posts.content` contains raw HTML (`<span class="post-anim-frame" ...>`) written by a moderator — find how it's rendered. If `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is used without sanitization, note that a compromised/moderator account can execute script in every member's MAX webview; assess severity honestly.
4. Client-side trust of role: search for authorization decisions made in the client (`role === 'moderator'`, `isModerator`, admin menus, `canComment`) and confirm which are backed by server rules and which only gate the UI.
5. Secrets/sensitive data in the bundle: fetch and grep the built JS (https://app.milenkih-team.ru/assets/*.js) and localStorage/sessionStorage contents for tokens, bot tokens, API keys, source maps, internal URLs. Also check for exposed `.map` files. Report only what is genuinely sensitive (not public IDs).
6. DOM-based XSS via URL/hash/query params and via postMessage handling (search `addEventListener('message'`, `window.location`, `location.hash`, `searchParams`, and the MAX bridge SDK wrapper in client/src/hooks/useMaxAuth.js / useMaxCloseGuard.js).
7. Client-side route/auth bypass: can a guest reach moderator-only views by manipulating `activeTab`/state, and does that grant any real capability?
Use agent-browser against the live site with your own session; do not create records unless needed, and if you do, prefix content with `zqath3` and clean up. Record coverage per surface and return a precise write-up via agent_finish with exact evidence (DOM proof, raw HTML response excerpt, file:line).

FOCUS: the `trainings` collection has `updateRule = '@request.auth.id != ""'` (any authenticated user may PATCH any training). The server-side guard is pb_hooks/trainingslib.js (assertTrainingUpdateAllowed + applyBookingSideEffects, invoked from pb_hooks/trainings_booking_validate.pb.js). Read that file carefully.
Hypotheses to validate (prove or refute each with exact raw requests/responses):
1. A plain user can PATCH another user's booking onto a training: body with booked_users containing a DIFFERENT user id. The code is supposed to throw ForbiddenError, but note `applyBookingSideEffects` is called AFTER assertTrainingUpdateAllowed and only rejects when `String(added[i]) !== authId` unless isModerator. Test whether a payload that mutates BOTH booked_users and unpaid_booked_users, or that exploits the `isCancelTransition`/`isRestoreTransition` branch (which SKIPS the "only yourself" check entirely), lets you modify other users' bookings. Concretely try: (a) flip is_cancelled false->true while also setting booked_users to arbitrary user ids; (b) flip is_cancelled true->false (restore) with arbitrary booked_users; (c) same-request combos.
2. Session abuse: can a user book then unbook repeatedly to manipulate their own available_sessions / unpaid_sessions / attendance_count? Compare users/{myid} fields before/after each attempt.
3. max_slots bypass: the seat-limit check uses `audit.newlyAdded([], record.get('booked_users')).length` — inspect whether a malformed booked_users value (string vs array, duplicates, null) bypasses it, and whether you can exceed max_slots.
4. Can a user cancel/close/delete other people's trainings or alter training metadata (date/location/max_slots) via PATCH despite the allow-list?

For every mutation you attempt, capture the user's before/after state and ALWAYS restore the record to its original state when a write succeeds (send the original field values back). Never leave a training cancelled or a booking altered. Use marker-free payload changes only for existing records; if you must create anything, prefix it `zqath3` and delete it after.

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / spoofed moderator notification (OWASP API5)
entries.evidence: Handler has no role check (only `if (!auth) 401`). It broadcasts to ALL moderators via bot.notifyModerators. `actorId` is bound to auth.id, but `actorIsModerator` is taken verbatim from the request body and `userIds` accepts arbitrary ids. A low-priv `user` token returns HTTP 200 {"success":true} with actorIsModerator=true and a foreign userId, producing text "Модератор <name> снял <foreign user> с тренировки" delivered to every moderator's MAX bot chat. Client only calls it with actorIsModerator=isModerator(), but the server never re-derives it.

entries.risk_area: Missing authentication on custom route (BFLA/API5)
entries.evidence: Route has NO `info.auth` check (unlike its siblings), confirmed live: unauthenticated GET returns 200 image/jpeg 54KB poster for posts record mz33mve1ouwipbv. BUT the underlying /api/files/posts/... file itself also returned 200 unauthenticated (73MB), so the poster route is not clearly the causal control. Needs confirmation whether anonymous file access is deployment-wide by design (broader finding) or whether video-poster exceeds the /api/files policy.

entries.risk_area: Authentication bypass / signature forgery
entries.evidence: Server implements the full MAX spec: hash-count==1 check, auth_date recency (|now-auth_date|<=300s), secret_key=HMAC-SHA256(key="WebAppData", data=BOT_TOKEN), signature=HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, sorted newline-joined launch_params), constant-time compare via $security.equal (pb_hooks/max-auth.pb.js:36-69, pb_hooks/maxauthlib.js:122-138). Fired 48+ generated initData variants signed with the real leaked MAX_BOT_TOKEN (client/.env) across key derivations (derived WebAppData-HMAC / raw token), signing algorithms (HMAC-SHA256 / SHA-256), separators (\\n / &), value modes (decoded / percent-encoded), and encodings (hex/HEX/base64) — ALL returned 401 {"error":"invalid signature"}. Missing/empty initData and non-string initData return 400. No unsigned or partially-verified path exists.

entries.risk_area: JWT forgery / algorithm confusion / claim tampering

entries.risk_area: Account enumeration via password-reset / verification flows

entries.risk_area: CORS misconfiguration / cross-origin data exposure
entries.evidence: Live OPTIONS preflight with Origin: https://evil-attacker.example returns 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * , Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization,content-type, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE (nginx configs in config/ set no CORS headers; this is PocketBase's default). No Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is sent, so cookie-borne credentials are NOT exposed, and the client uses a bearer header (pb.authStore.token), not cookies — so classic CSRF is not possible; impact is token-exfiltration amplification. Reported as low-severity hardening finding.

entries.risk_area: Session revocation / token invalidation on refresh & logout
entries.evidence: POST /api/collections/users/auth-refresh with header Authorization: T0 returned a NEW token T1 (differs) while T0 continued to authenticate (200) — refresh does not rotate/invalidate. No /api/collections/users/logout or /auth-logout endpoint exists (404). The client's only "logout" is pb.authStore.clear() (localStorage only; src/services/auth.js finalizeBannedUser, src/hooks/useMaxAuth.js:152). Revocation does occur on ban via tokenKey rotation (pb_hooks/users_ban_auth.pb.js:22-28). Impact is session-management weakness, mitigated by browser localStorage same-origin isolation — low severity, no attacker path without an already-stolen token.

entries.risk_area: MAX Bridge initData wire-format / signature reconstruction
entries.evidence: Read pb_hooks/maxauthlib.js in full and validated its HMAC-SHA256/SHA-256 implementation against Node.js crypto on 8 inputs including key lengths 63/64/65/128 (the HMAC block-boundary and key>block pre-hash cases) and non-ASCII UTF-8 messages — 0 mismatches; the production secret_key HMAC-SHA256("WebAppData", MAX_BOT_TOKEN) = 82adbd35a2daf2eba8f24dd382c9872bc4cebacf7a7d7090fd042ce42fc0cb8b reproduced exactly. Server-side crypto is correct, but the exact byte-string the live backend signs could NOT be reproduced from its own source, so the precise initData wire format remains an open proof gap.

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization on custom hook routes
entries.evidence: Tested as a plain `user` token against every custom route. All return a role check before any side effect: /api/bot-notify-training-status|edit|cancelled|restored|create -> 403; /api/users-claim-candidates|claim-max|unclaim-max -> 403; /api/users-create-manual -> 403; /api/admin-backup -> 403; /api/admin-dispatch-now -> 403; /api/users-delete -> 403; /api/system-templates -> 403; /api/internal/backup-notify -> 403. entries.surface: PocketBase users collection — GET /api/collections/users/records (list) and /records/{id} (view) as low-priv user
entries.risk_area: API1 BOLA / broken object-level authorization + sensitive field over-exposure

entries.surface: trainings collection — PATCH /api/collections/trainings/records/{id} as low-priv user (booking side-effects hook)

entries.risk_area: API1 BOLA / anonymous access to authenticated-only collections
entries.evidence: Anonymous GET /api/collections/users/records?perPage=1 -> 200 with totalItems=0 (no data), while the same request authenticated returns 4 records — public access is a filter-empty artifact with no rows leaked for users. Anonymous GET /api/collections/product_categories/records does return the 7 public catalog rows by design (listRule=''). entries.risk_area: API1 BOLA write — PATCH/PUT/DELETE foreign records in users, product_categories, products, achievement_levels, product_param_templates, achievement/level meta collections

entries.surface: Likes collections — post_likes, comment_likes, gallery_likes (create/update/delete + own-record read)

entries.surface: notifications collection — list/view/create/update/delete of foreign recipients

entries.risk_area: IDOR / broken object-level authorization

Verified with a non-existent id, a real other user id (i9l04znh39u9iy4), and mixed [self,victim] payloads, all 403. Also holds under 8-way concurrency and on the max_slots=4 training.

entries.risk_area: Broken object property-level authorization (cross-user history forgery)

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / unauthorized metadata modification
entries.evidence: Non-moderator PATCH of date, location, max_slots, duration, type, description, is_closed, is_deleted and is_cancelled all returned 403 'Изменение поля "<f>" недоступно' — assertTrainingUpdateAllowed (pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:355-371) runs before the booking check and rejects every field outside TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE. entries.surface: trainings self book/unbook session accounting (available_sessions, unpaid_sessions, used_sessions)
entries.risk_area: Business logic / session-counter manipulation

entries.risk_area: Business logic / seat-limit bypass
entries.evidence: Seat check `audit.newlyAdded([], record.get('booked_users')).length > max_slots` held for duplicates (5x same id -> PB deduped to 1), string, null, object, empty-then-me, nested array, NUL/comma/space-joined strings, and 4-way concurrent PATCH on a max_slots=4 training. Malformed values either fail PB relation validation (403/400) or normalize to <=1 entry.

entries.risk_area: Race condition / TOCTOU on session decrement and last-seat
entries.evidence: Concurrent PATCH bursts (8 identical, 4 distinct) produced exactly one set of side effects; $app.runInTransaction in applyBookingSideEffects serializes the read-modify-write on users. No double-decrement, no over-issue, no lost update observed across repeated runs.

entries.surface: PATCH trainings — is_cancelled false->true / true->false (cancel/restore transition bypass)
entries.risk_area: Authorization bypass via state-transition branch
entries.evidence: Closed by correlating the peer's result with mine rather than leaving it open. The peer concluded the cancel/restore branches (trainingslib.js:437-483) are "unreachable for a non-privileged user" because is_cancelled is not in TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE and assertTrainingUpdateAllowed rejects it. My testing confirms the rejection is real but shows WHY: the wrapper at trainingslib.js:395 means assertTrainingUpdateAllowed is the only thing that stops it, and it rejects on the field name rather than on the transition. Live differential on qs808160ey9ib5q with the user token: {"is_cancelled":true,"attended_users":[self]} -> 403 naming is_cancelled; {"booked_users":[self]} -> 200 vs {"booked_users":[self,other]} -> 403 "Можно записать только себя". So the guard at 395-413 does execute, and it does not evaluate attended_users inside a cancel transition; the two layers share one client-controlled precondition. The isCancelTransition branch itself I also could not land: of 25 consecutive attempts at {"is_cancelled":true,"booked_users":[]} every reply was 403 or 502, never 200, while no-change bodies returned 200 immediately. Net: this is a genuine defect (removable authorization control + a traced write to users.attendance_count at line 491), correctly downgraded to Low because the counter increment was never observed and the only reachable training has already ended (if (!ended) at line 473 skips it). Full detail, the exact differential, the regression commit and the proposed patch are on the shared note titled "FINDING (primary): trainingslib.js:395 guard gated on client-supplied is_cancelled". Root-cause-idor-trainingslib395 is an OPEN PROOF GAP for the end-to-end write only.

(so 'author != @request.auth.id' injection is blocked), filter=is_banned=true returns 0 rows, and no filter allowed elevating the result set beyond the already-permitted listRule. fields=*,email and fields=id,email,max_id,... returned exactly the same fields as the unfiltered record — no hidden field is reachable only through projection. Non-existent ids return 404 uniformly for unauthenticated/bad tokens.

entries.surface: content_views — list/view/delete of other users' view rows
entries.risk_area: API1 BOLA — reading or writing other users' view-tracking rows

(list/viewRule null) and no create/update/delete path exists (createRule only allows user = @request.auth.id but the resulting self-row is unreadable and undeletable, DELETE -> 403). I created one self-row (vo799p1968ejh57) to confirm the create path and could not delete it — noted as an inability to clean up because the rule itself denies deletion to all non-superusers.

entries.risk_area: API1 BOLA — unauthorized file reads (avatars, gallery, product images)

entries.risk_area: Stored XSS into other users' in-app notifications
entries.evidence: Server-side hook (pb_hooks/comment_replies_lib.js) writes an in-app `notifications` record with title=actor full_name, body=parent comment text (stripHtmlToPlain strips tags), badge_text=reply text, meta with raw actor.full_name/avatar_url. User-controlled input DOES reach these fields, but: (a) a normal user cannot change full_name (PATCH full_name -> 403 "Изменение поля full_name недоступно" via users_access_guard_lib.js SELF_EDITABLE_ALWAYS allow-list, which also blocks can_comment/is_visible/max_id/rating_points), so the name vector is closed; (b) comment text is HTML-stripped before storage; (c) POST self-notification succeeded (200, id k4p4l299ke15ey7) but only self-addressed, while recipient=OTHER was rejected (400 "Failed to create record", createRule @request.auth.id != "" && (recipient = @request.auth.id || role = moderator)); read list is self-scoped (totalItems: 2, all mine). The only exposure is self-XSS requiring the victim to write their own comment. Probe record deleted (204).

entries.surface: users auth collection endpoints (auth-with-password / otp / oauth2 / reset / impersonate)
entries.risk_area: Weak passwords / auth endpoint misconfiguration / account enumeration
entries.evidence: Probed every auth endpoint. auth-with-password exists and is enabled (returns 400 "Failed to authenticate." for any wrong password, incl. the correct email of the real account); OTP returns 403 "not configured to allow OTP authentication"; OAuth2 returns 403 "not configured to allow OAuth2 authentication"; confirm-password-reset validates the token (400 validation_invalid_token); /users/impersonate 404; /_superusers/auth-with-password exists (separate superuser collection). No endpoint leaked account existence (request-password-reset uniform 204/timing; auth-with-password uniform 400). ~2 wrong-password attempts total, well under budget; no brute force performed.

entries.risk_area: Server-side template injection via interpolate()/resolve()
entries.evidence: Ran templatelib.js under Node with PocketBase globals stubbed. `interpolate(text,vars)` splits on `{{k}}` for each key of `vars` and joins — a single pass with no re-scan. Injecting `{{time}}`/`{{name}}`/`{{count}}` via a user-controlled `full_name` (the `actor` var) survives verbatim into the output and is never expanded. `${7*7}`, `%s` and HTML also pass through unmodified. resolve() call sites all pass compile-time literal keys (grep of bot_notifications.pb.js, comment_replies_lib.js, mention_notifications_lib.js, notification libs). Confirms the two-pass template expansion hypothesis is impossible; the residual concern is only stored markup in a MAX markdown message or a React-rendered card.

entries.risk_area: Stored XSS via injected markup in notification title/body
entries.evidence: Client render path traced: NotificationCard.jsx renders notification.title/body through PostContentHtml -> toDisplayHtml() in client/src/features/feed/postRichText.js, a DOMParser-based allow-list sanitizer (tags B/STRONG/I/EM/U/A/BR/DIV/P/SPAN/IMG; per-tag attribute allow-list; href must match ^https?:// or mailto:; IMG src must match ^https?://|/|data:image/; all attribute values escapeHtml'd). A plain-string actor name such as `` fails looksLikeRichHtml() and is fully escapeHtml'd, so no tag survives. The comment/mention path stores only the actor name as a literal string, not attacker HTML. No bypass found.

entries.risk_area: API3 Broken object property level authorization (over-exposure)
entries.evidence: With a plain `user` token, GET /api/collections/users/records (list) and /records/{otherId} (view) return every other member's private fields: email (or `null` when the member hid it), max_id, birth_date, membership_start_date/end_date/type, available_sessions, used_sessions, unpaid_sessions, rating_points, attendance_count, ban_reason, membership_frozen, avatar_url. The collection rule is `@request.auth.id != ""` for both list and view, so this applies to every member. Confirmed by reading both the own and a moderator's record. This is a pre-existing over-exposure of member PII/financial data in the schema's design, not something introduced by the tested hook code, and it is likely intended for the app's member directory (client/src/services/users.js requests a narrower `fields` set: id,collectionId,collectionName,full_name,avatar,avatar_url), which suggests the unrestricted read is not needed by the SPA.

entries.surface: users collection self-update + client-side rating_points increment
entries.risk_area: Self-service privilege escalation / server-authoritative value forgery (rating, attendance, membership)
entries.evidence: Tested the client-side `applyTournamentPostSideEffects` path (client/src/services/tournamentPosts.js:244-252) which calls `pb.collection('users').update(userId, {'rating_points+': points})` directly from the browser, duplicating the server hook. entries.risk_area: JSON/prototype pollution in participants handling; achievement progress forgery
entries.evidence: Read achievementslib.js parseParticipants and exercised it under Node with hostile inputs: `__proto__`/`constructor.prototype` payloads, string/number/object instead of array, nested arrays, string and negative and 1e308 place values, null elements, object-typed userId. parseParticipants returns [] for every non-array shape, `Object.prototype` remains unpolluted, and countUserTournamentPlacesFromPosts counts only the FIRST matching entry per post (so duplicate entries cannot inflate counts). Combined with `achievements`/`achievement_levels`/`tournament_posts` all being moderator-write, and rating_points being denied by the field ACL, no forgery path exists from a member account.

entries.risk_area: SSRF / path traversal / CRLF header injection
entries.evidence: SSRF: /api/yadisk-preview enforces auth (401 anonymous) and an allowlist regex ^https?://(disk.yandex.(ru|com(.tr)?)|yadi.sk)/(i|d|a|public)/ — tested http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health, https://example.com, https://disk.yandex.ru@127.0.0.1/i/x (userinfo confusion) and HTTP://DISK.YANDEX.RU/i/x; all non-Yandex forms returned 400 'Некорректная ссылка Яндекс.Диска' and only the canonical host was forwarded. /api/yadisk-content additionally returns 401 anonymously. entries.surface: pb_hooks filter construction (all findRecordsByFilter call sites)
entries.risk_area: PocketBase filter injection via string concatenation
entries.evidence: Swept every `findRecordsByFilter`/`findFirstRecordByFilter` call site in pb_hooks. All filter strings are built from server-derived values only: templatelib uses compile-time literal keys ('key = "' + d.key + '"'), achievementslib uses numeric sort_order and moderator-written achievement ids, statslib dates pass a strict /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ check in parsePeriod before use, notificationslib/mention_notifications_lib/comment_replies_lib interpolate record-derived recipient/author ids, and claimlib binds the one user-supplied value through the `{:exclude}` parameter form. No attacker-controlled string is concatenated into a PocketBase filter, so filter breakout (quote/`||`/`&&`/`@request.auth`) is not reachable.

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level & object-level authorization: attendance (attended_users) and other-member booking writes
entries.evidence: Guard at pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:395 is gated on `if (!isCancelTransition && !isRestoreTransition)`, and both flags come from the client-supplied `is_cancelled` (lines 387-388). Live: PATCH {"is_cancelled":true,"attended_users":[self]} -> 403 naming is_cancelled and NOT attended_users; PATCH {"booked_users":[self]} -> 200 vs {"booked_users":[other]} -> 403 proves newlyAdded is the trigger, i.e. the same code path is reachable. assertTrainingUpdateAllowed (line 359) does not compensate: attended_users is absent from TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE (lines 304-310). Regression: efaa612 (v1.0.18) added the field ACL in front of a side-effect function that still carries the broken derived-flag guard.

entries.risk_area: Mass assignment / privilege escalation (rating_points, attendance_count, role, membership, sessions)
entries.evidence: Blocked by the field allow-list in pb_hooks/users_access_guard_lib.js:119-153 (SELF_EDITABLE_ALWAYS at lines 6-16) invoked from pb_hooks/users_access_guard.pb.js:15-33 on every non-privileged update. Live 403 for rating_points, attendance_count, role, is_visible-free membership fields: {"message":"Изменение поля \"rating_points\" недоступно."}. The guard compares original vs record with NUMBER_FIELDS/BOOL_FIELDS-aware comparison (lines 81-97), so arithmetic operators (`rating_points+`) and type coercion do not evade it.

entries.risk_area: BFLA / privilege escalation via granting achievement levels
entries.evidence: schema.json createRule/updateRule/deleteRule = `@request.auth.role = "moderator"` for both collections. Live with a role=user token: POST /api/collections/achievements/records -> 400 "Failed to create record."; PATCH/DELETE on an existing achievement id -> 404; same for achievement_levels. No 2xx response was ever returned. Moderator-only writes are therefore enforced at the collection rule, before any hook.

entries.risk_area: BFLA on custom pb_hooks routerAdd endpoints; forged achievement state
entries.evidence: Enumerated all routerAdd endpoints in pb_hooks (stats.pb.js, admin_scheduler.pb.js, backup.pb.js, bot_notifications.pb.js, user*_claim/manual/delete.pb.js, yadisk.pb.js, video_poster.pb.js, max-auth.pb.js, shop_audit.pb.js, comment_replies.pb.js, membership_lifecycle.pb.js). Every /api/stats/* route calls stats.requireModerator(c) first (stats.pb.js:28,44,60,86,102,118,138,158,172); /api/admin-dispatch-now, /api/admin-backup and the /api/bot-notify-* routes each check `auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator'`. /api/content-view and /api/max-auth are intentionally auth-only. entries.risk_area: Forged mention notifications: user-regex/server-regex differential in extractUserMentionIds

So the guard at 395-413 does execute, and it does not evaluate attended_users inside a cancel transition; the two layers share one client-controlled precondition. The isCancelTransition branch itself I also could not land: of 25 consecutive attempts at {"is_cancelled":true,"booked_users":[]} every reply was 403 or 502, never 200, while no-change bodies returned 200 immediately. Net: this is a genuine defect (removable authorization control + a traced write to users.attendance_count at line 491), correctly downgraded to Low because the counter increment was never observed and the only reachable training has already ended (if (!ended) at line 473 skips it). gaps.risk_area: Forged mention notifications: user-regex/server-regex differential in extractUserMentionIds
gaps.detail: Traced the mention pipeline: server-side `extractUserMentionIds` in pb_hooks/mention_notifications_lib.js scans `<span ...>` tags in comments.text/posts.content and regex-extracts the first `data-user-id` per tag, then creates a notification for each id (mention_notifications.pb.js fires on create/update). Modelled it in node against sanitized output: a user-controlled floating `data-user-id="X"` before the real attributes is preserved verbatim by the client sanitizer (which re-emits the FIRST `data-user-id` it finds) and parsed by the server regex, so a member could point a mention chip at a spoofed user id and trigger a notification to an arbitrary real user with forged mention copy. The impact is the same class of forged-notification spoofing already filed as vuln-0007 for the notifications collection, and the written evidence is a source+regex model rather than a live end-to-end replay (I did not fire it at a real user's inbox). Recording the gap rather than claiming it.
